text: Given a pending ThreatLocker approval request id, When the agent calls threatlocker_approvals_approve with that id, Then the result names the approval request id and action: approve
Given a non-existent or already-resolved approval request id, When threatlocker_approvals_approve is called, Then it returns a structured error envelope, not an exception
Given a pending approval request id and a reason, When the agent calls threatlocker_approvals_reject, Then the result names the approval request id and action: reject
Given an approval request id that ApprovalRequestGetById 404s on, When threatlocker_approvals_reject is called, Then it returns a not_found envelope and never calls the reject endpoint
Given a pending approval request id and a reason, When the agent calls threatlocker_approvals_ignore, Then the result names the approval request id and action: ignore
Given an approval request id that ApprovalRequestGetById 404s on, When threatlocker_approvals_ignore is called, Then it returns a not_found envelope and never calls the ignore endpoint
Given a syntactically invalid GUID, When any of approve/reject/ignore is called with it, Then it returns invalid_argument without making any HTTP call to ThreatLocker
Given a known ringfencing policy id, When the agent calls threatlocker_ringfence_get, Then it returns that policy's data
Given an unknown ringfencing policy id, When the agent calls threatlocker_ringfence_get, Then it returns a not_found error envelope
Given valid credentials, When the agent calls threatlocker_ringfence_eligibility, Then it returns the organization's Ringfencing eligibility
Given an organization not yet enrolled in Ringfencing, When the agent calls threatlocker_ringfence_opt_in, Then it returns a success result naming action: opt_in

Given an organization already enrolled in Ringfencing, When the agent calls threatlocker_ringfence_opt_in again, Then the tool returns whatever ThreatLocker reports (success/no-op/error) without crashing
steps: Use a real ThreatLocker vendor test organization already enrolled in Ringfencing
Call POST /mcp tools/call threatlocker_ringfence_opt_in with that organization's credentials
Inspect the HTTP status and tool response
expect: Tool returns a JSON result (success, no-op, or a structured error envelope) — no unhandled exception, no 5xx from the MCP server itself
evidence: needs a real vendor account; not run in this design/dev pass per mcp-track.md section 2.5 (missing test account is not a blocker)

text: Given a call to any of the 6 new tools with no ThreatLocker headers, When the tool runs, Then it returns the same not_configured envelope the existing read tools return

Given two sequential calls with two different X-Threatlocker-Organization-Id values, When either calls approve/reject/ignore/opt_in, Then each call's ManagedOrganizationId header equals only that call's own organization id, never the other tenant's
Given any of the 6 new tools succeeds, When its result is returned, Then the result includes the id acted on and the action name (no silently empty success result)
Given the updated server, When tools/list is called, Then all 17 existing tool names keep their existing required parameters and the 6 new tool names are present
